```{r sec4-dist-plots, results='asis', fig.height=6}
  }

  if (!is.null(pct_shared_data) && nrow(pct_shared_data) > 0) {
    p1 <- ggplot(pct_shared_data[!is.na(pct_shared_data$pct_shared), ],
                 aes(x = pct_shared, fill = comparison)) +
      geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
      theme_minimal() +
      labs(title = "Sequence Shared (%): NMD vs Control (all_samples)",
           subtitle = "NMD shifted right = more similar (targeted changes)",
           x = "pct_shared", y = "Density", fill = "")
    print(p1)
    cat("\n\n")
  }

}
```

# 5. PTC & Reading Frame

```{r sec5-ptc-compute}
# Compute PTC rates for all_samples (used by inline references and display chunk below)
ptc_rows <- compute_ptc_rates_row("all_samples")
if (!is.null(ptc_rows)) rownames(ptc_rows) <- NULL
ptc_or_range <- if (!is.null(ptc_rows)) {
  or_vals <- ptc_rows$fisher_OR[!is.na(ptc_rows$fisher_OR)]
  sprintf("OR %s", round(or_vals[1]))
} else {
  "OR N/A"
}
ctrl_ptc_pcts <- if (!is.null(ptc_rows)) {
  round(ptc_rows$Ctrl_comp_ptc_pct[1])
} else {
  5
}
```

PTC enrichment (`r ptc_or_range`) is the single strongest signal distinguishing NMD-sensitive isoform
pairs from baseline structural variation. At baseline, ~`r ctrl_ptc_pcts`% of non-NMD comparator isoforms
contain a PTC. Reading frame is compared independently for each isoform at shared CDS regions,
distinguishing splicing-induced frameshifts (same start codon) from alternative initiation
(different start codons). NMD departs dramatically from Control in both PTC prevalence and
the consequences of frame disruption.

## PTC Rates

Premature termination codons (PTCs) are stop codons located >50 nucleotides upstream of the
last exon-exon junction, a position that triggers nonsense-mediated decay. This table compares
PTC prevalence in NMD comparator isoforms vs Control comparator isoforms, restricted to
**coding pairs** (both reference and comparator have a SQANTI CDS annotation). Non-coding
isoforms cannot harbour a PTC and are excluded from both the numerator and denominator.

PTC status is determined per-isoform using each isoform's own CDS (`computePtcStatus()` in
`Isopair/R/ptc.R`; see METHODS.md §Reading Frame and PTC Analysis). The 50-nt rule is
applied to each isoform's stop codon relative to its own last exon-exon junction.

**Columns:** **n_coding_pairs** = pairs where both reference and comparator are coding;
**NMD_comp_ptc_n / NMD_comp_ptc_pct** = number and % of NMD comparators with a PTC
(among coding pairs); **Ctrl_comp_ptc_n / Ctrl_comp_ptc_pct** = same for Control;
**fisher_OR** = odds ratio from Fisher's exact test (>1 = enriched in NMD);
**p_value** = Fisher's exact test p-value.

```{r sec5-ptc-rates, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(ptc_rows)) {
  knitr::kable(ptc_rows, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = "PTC Rates: NMD vs Control Comparators (coding pairs only)") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Reading Frame Comparison

For each isoform pair, we compare the reading frame at shared CDS regions using each
isoform's own CDS annotation independently (`compareIsoformFrames()` in
`Isopair/R/ptc.R`; see METHODS.md §Reading Frame and PTC Analysis). CDS exon intervals
are extracted per isoform from the SQANTI GFF3 (`extractCdsExons()` in
`Isopair/R/annotate-regions.R`). For each pair, the function identifies genomic intervals
where both isoforms have CDS coverage, then computes the CDS phase (cumulative coding
bp mod 3) independently for each isoform at the 5' end of each shared interval.

The analysis first determines whether the two isoforms share the same start codon
(translation initiation site, with tolerance = 0), then evaluates whether shared CDS
regions are translated in the same reading frame. Every pair is assigned to exactly one
of six categories:

### Frame Category Counts

Each pair is classified into one of the following categories. The first four apply to
coding pairs with overlapping CDS; the last two are excluded from frame-specific analyses.

- **same_start_in_frame**: Both isoforms begin translation at the same position. All
  shared CDS regions are read in the same phase. Splicing differences between these
  isoforms affect sequence content but preserve the reading frame.
- **same_start_frameshift**: Both isoforms begin translation at the same position, but
  a splicing difference (e.g., a non-divisible-by-3 exon skip or boundary shift) causes
  downstream shared CDS to be read in a different phase. This is a splicing-induced
  frameshift.
- **diff_start_same_frame**: The two isoforms use different translation initiation
  sites, but shared CDS regions are read in the same phase (the start codon offset is a
  multiple of 3, or compensating splicing restores phase). No frameshift is implied.
- **diff_start_diff_frame**: The two isoforms use different translation initiation
  sites, and shared CDS regions are read in different phases with a constant phase offset.
  The frame difference is entirely attributable to the initiation site difference — all
  internal splicing differences are multiples of 3 (no frameshift).
- **diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift**: The two isoforms use different translation
  initiation sites, and the phase offset between them changes across shared CDS regions.
  This indicates a splicing-induced frameshift on top of the start codon offset.
- **non_coding**: One or both isoforms lack a CDS annotation (SQANTI coding_status ≠
  "coding"). These pairs cannot be evaluated for reading frame.
- **no_shared_cds**: Both isoforms are coding, but their CDS regions do not overlap
  genomically (e.g., entirely different exons are coding). No shared interval exists for
  phase comparison.

**Columns:** **cell_type** = cell type; **frame_category** = classification (see above);
**NMD_n / NMD_pct** = count and percentage of NMD (C2) pairs in this category;
**Ctrl_n / Ctrl_pct** = count and percentage of Control (C4) pairs. Percentages are
computed over all pairs in the respective set (including non_coding and no_shared_cds).

```{r sec5-frame-comp-detail, results='asis'}
# Detailed breakdown of frame categories — all_samples only
fc_detail <- compute_frame_category_rows("all_samples")
if (!is.null(fc_detail)) {
  widget <- datatable(fc_detail, caption = "Frame Category Counts: NMD vs Control (all_samples)",
                      rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe",
                      options = list(pageLength = nrow(fc_detail), dom = 'ft'))
  rendered <- htmltools::renderTags(widget)
  knitr::knit_meta_add(rendered$dependencies)
  cat(rendered$html)
  cat("\n")
}
```

```{r sec5-frame-comp-barchart, results='asis', fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
if (!is.null(fc_detail) && has_ggplot2) {
  coding_cats <- c("same_start_in_frame", "same_start_frameshift",
                   "diff_start_same_frame", "diff_start_diff_frame",
                   "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift")
  cat_labels <- c(
    same_start_in_frame = "Same Start\nSame Frame",
    same_start_frameshift = "Same Start\nFrameshift",
    diff_start_same_frame = "Diff Start\nSame Frame",
    diff_start_diff_frame = "Diff Start\nDiff Frame",
    diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift = "Diff Start\nDiff Frame + FS"
  )

  ptc_pos_ids <- ptc$isoform_id[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE]

  # Build stacked data: PTC+ and No PTC per category × comparison (all_samples only)
  stacked_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("c2", "c4"), function(comp) {
    key <- paste0(comp, "_allsamples")
    fc <- set_results[[key]]$frame_comp
    if (is.null(fc)) return(NULL)
    ps <- fc$pair_summary
    total_pairs <- nrow(set_results[[key]]$profiles)
    comp_lbl <- if (comp == "c2") "NMD" else "Control"

    do.call(rbind, lapply(coding_cats, function(cat) {
      cat_pairs <- ps[ps$frame_category == cat, ]
      n_cat <- nrow(cat_pairs)
      n_ptc <- sum(cat_pairs$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc_pos_ids)
      n_no_ptc <- n_cat - n_ptc
      pct_ptc <- 100 * n_ptc / max(total_pairs, 1)
      pct_no_ptc <- 100 * n_no_ptc / max(total_pairs, 1)

      rbind(
        data.frame(frame_category = cat,
                   category_label = cat_labels[cat],
                   comparison = comp_lbl, ptc_status = "PTC+",
                   n = n_ptc, pct = pct_ptc),
        data.frame(frame_category = cat,
                   category_label = cat_labels[cat],
                   comparison = comp_lbl, ptc_status = "No PTC",
                   n = n_no_ptc, pct = pct_no_ptc)
      )
    }))
  }))

  stacked_df$category_label <- factor(stacked_df$category_label,
    levels = cat_labels[coding_cats])
  stacked_df$ptc_status <- factor(stacked_df$ptc_status, levels = c("PTC+", "No PTC"))

  stacked_df$fill_group <- paste(stacked_df$comparison, stacked_df$ptc_status, sep = " - ")
  stacked_df$fill_group <- factor(stacked_df$fill_group,
    levels = c("NMD - No PTC", "NMD - PTC+", "Control - No PTC", "Control - PTC+"))

  bar_totals <- aggregate(cbind(n, pct) ~ frame_category + category_label + comparison,
                          data = stacked_df, FUN = sum)

  # Fisher's test per category
  p_labels <- do.call(rbind, lapply(coding_cats, function(cat) {
    n_c2 <- fc_detail$NMD_n[fc_detail$frame_category == cat]
    n_c4 <- fc_detail$Ctrl_n[fc_detail$frame_category == cat]
    total_c2 <- sum(fc_detail$NMD_n)
    total_c4 <- sum(fc_detail$Ctrl_n)
    ft <- tryCatch({
      mat <- matrix(c(n_c2, total_c2 - n_c2, n_c4, total_c4 - n_c4), nrow = 2)
      fisher.test(mat)
    }, error = function(e) list(p.value = NA))
    p <- ft$p.value
    stars <- if (is.na(p)) "" else if (p < 0.001) "***" else if (p < 0.01) "**" else if (p < 0.05) "*" else "ns"
    max_pct <- max(bar_totals$pct[bar_totals$frame_category == cat], na.rm = TRUE)
    data.frame(category_label = cat_labels[cat],
               p_star = stars, max_pct = max_pct)
  }))
  p_labels$category_label <- factor(p_labels$category_label,
    levels = cat_labels[coding_cats])

  p_bar <- ggplot(stacked_df, aes(x = comparison, y = pct, fill = fill_group)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = bar_totals, aes(x = comparison, y = pct, label = n, fill = NULL),
              vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = p_labels, aes(x = 1.5, y = max_pct + 4, label = p_star),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
    facet_wrap(~ category_label, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("NMD - No PTC" = "#ef8a62", "NMD - PTC+" = "#8c2d04",
                 "Control - No PTC" = "#67a9cf", "Control - PTC+" = "#2166ac"),
      name = NULL,
      labels = c("NMD - No PTC" = "NMD (No PTC)", "NMD - PTC+" = "NMD (PTC+)",
                 "Control - No PTC" = "Control (No PTC)", "Control - PTC+" = "Control (PTC+)")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of all pairs",
         title = "Frame Category Distribution: NMD vs Control (all_samples)",
         subtitle = "Stacked by PTC status. Numbers above bars = total pair counts. *** p<0.001, ** p<0.01, * p<0.05, ns (Fisher's exact test)")
  print(p_bar)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### PTC Mechanism Breakdown

For PTC-containing comparator isoforms, what is the mechanism by which the PTC arises?
Each PTC+ comparator is classified by its frame category, revealing the route to premature
termination:

- **Same start, frameshift**: Splicing disrupts the reading frame, creating a premature stop
  downstream of the frameshift boundary.
- **Same start, in-frame**: PTC exists within the original reading frame (e.g., a retained
  intron containing a stop codon, or an exon skip that joins in-frame segments with a stop
  between them).
- **Diff start, same frame**: Alternative translation initiation, but shared CDS regions
  are read in the same phase — PTC arises from the shorter or different ORF.
- **Diff start, diff frame**: Alternative initiation reads shared CDS in a different phase.
- **Diff start, diff frame + FS**: Alternative initiation plus an additional splicing-induced
  frameshift.

The table and figure show these mechanism frequencies for both NMD and Control PTC+
comparators. A Fisher's exact test for splicing-induced frameshift enrichment among
same-start pairs is also reported, since this is the primary NMD-generating mechanism.

**PTC Mechanism table columns:** **frame_category** = reading frame classification of
the isoform pair (see §Frame Category Counts above); **NMD_n / NMD_pct** = number and
% of NMD PTC+ comparators in this category; **Ctrl_n / Ctrl_pct** = same for Control.
Percentages are of all PTC+ comparators in each set.

**Frameshift Enrichment table columns:** **cell_type** = cell type;
**NMD_ss_total / Ctrl_ss_total** = total same-start coding pairs (in-frame + frameshift)
in NMD / Control; **NMD_fs_pct / Ctrl_fs_pct** = % of same-start pairs that are
frameshifted; **OR** = odds ratio from Fisher's exact test (>1 = frameshift enriched
in NMD); **p_value** = Fisher's exact test p-value.

```{r sec5-ptc-mechanism, results='asis', fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
coding_cats <- c("same_start_in_frame", "same_start_frameshift",
                 "diff_start_same_frame", "diff_start_diff_frame",
                 "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift")
mech_labels <- c(
  same_start_in_frame = "Same Start\nIn Frame",
  same_start_frameshift = "Same Start\nFrameshift",
  diff_start_same_frame = "Diff Start\nSame Frame",
  diff_start_diff_frame = "Diff Start\nDiff Frame",
  diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift = "Diff Start\nDiff Frame + FS"
)

mech_result <- compute_ptc_mechanism_rows("all_samples")
mech_rows <- mech_result$mechanism
fs_test_rows <- mech_result$fs_test

if (!is.null(mech_rows)) {
  nmd  <- mech_rows[mech_rows$comparison == "NMD", ]
  ctrl <- mech_rows[mech_rows$comparison == "Control", ]
  if (nrow(nmd) > 0 && nrow(ctrl) > 0) {
    mech_wide <- data.frame(
      frame_category = nmd$frame_category,
      NMD_n = nmd$n_ptc, NMD_pct = nmd$pct_of_ptc,
      Ctrl_n = ctrl$n_ptc, Ctrl_pct = ctrl$pct_of_ptc
    )
    rownames(mech_wide) <- NULL
    knitr::kable(mech_wide, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "PTC Mechanism: Frame Category of PTC+ Comparators (NMD vs Control, all_samples)") |> print()
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}

if (!is.null(fs_test_rows)) {
  rownames(fs_test_rows) <- NULL
  knitr::kable(fs_test_rows, row.names = FALSE,
    caption = "Splicing-Induced Frameshift Enrichment (Same-Start Pairs): NMD vs Control (all_samples)") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")
}

# --- Bar chart: PTC mechanism distribution (all_samples only) ---
if (!is.null(mech_rows) && has_ggplot2) {
  mech_rows$category_label <- factor(mech_labels[mech_rows$frame_category],
                                     levels = mech_labels[coding_cats])

  # Fisher's test per category
  p_labels <- do.call(rbind, lapply(coding_cats, function(cat) {
    nmd_r  <- mech_rows[mech_rows$comparison == "NMD", ]
    ctrl_r <- mech_rows[mech_rows$comparison == "Control", ]
    n_nmd <- nmd_r$n_ptc[nmd_r$frame_category == cat]
    t_nmd <- nmd_r$ptc_total[nmd_r$frame_category == cat]
    n_ctrl <- ctrl_r$n_ptc[ctrl_r$frame_category == cat]
    t_ctrl <- ctrl_r$ptc_total[ctrl_r$frame_category == cat]
    if (length(n_nmd) == 0 || length(n_ctrl) == 0) return(NULL)

    ft <- tryCatch({
      mat <- matrix(c(n_nmd, t_nmd - n_nmd, n_ctrl, t_ctrl - n_ctrl), nrow = 2)
      fisher.test(mat)
    }, error = function(e) list(p.value = NA))
    p <- ft$p.value
    stars <- if (is.na(p)) "" else if (p < 0.001) "***" else if (p < 0.01) "**" else if (p < 0.05) "*" else "ns"
    max_pct <- max(mech_rows$pct_of_ptc[mech_rows$frame_category == cat], na.rm = TRUE)
    data.frame(category_label = mech_labels[cat],
               p_star = stars, max_pct = max_pct)
  }))
  p_labels$category_label <- factor(p_labels$category_label, levels = mech_labels[coding_cats])

  p_mech <- ggplot(mech_rows, aes(x = comparison, y = pct_of_ptc, fill = comparison)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n_ptc), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = p_labels, aes(x = 1.5, y = max_pct + 5, label = p_star),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
    facet_wrap(~ category_label, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("NMD" = "#ef8a62", "Control" = "#67a9cf"), name = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of PTC+ comparators",
         title = "PTC Mechanism: How Do PTCs Arise? (all_samples)",
         subtitle = "Distribution of PTC+ comparators across frame categories. Numbers = pair counts. *** p<0.001, ** p<0.01, * p<0.05 (Fisher's exact test)")
  print(p_mech)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### Frameshift-Causing Events by Frame Category

Which splicing event types cause the frameshifts in each frame category? Using the frame
walk analysis (`walkFrameAlongEvents()` in `Isopair/R/ptc.R`), each CDS-overlapping event
is flagged as `is_frameshift = TRUE` when its CDS overlap is not divisible by 3. This table
and chart show the distribution of frameshift-causing event types within each frame category,
for both NMD and Control.

Only pairs in frame categories that involve a frameshift are shown (`same_start_frameshift`,
`diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift`). For `same_start_in_frame` and
`diff_start_same_frame` pairs, no events cause frameshifts by definition.

**Columns:** **frame_category** = reading frame classification; **comparison** = NMD or
Control; **event_type** = the splicing event type causing the frameshift;
**n_fs_events** = number of frameshift-causing events of this type;
**pct_of_fs_events** = % of all frameshift-causing events in this frame category and
comparison group.

```{r sec5-fs-causing-events, results='asis', fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
# Frame categories with frameshifts
fs_frame_cats <- c("same_start_frameshift",
                   "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift")

# Build table: for each frame category × comparison, which event types cause frameshifts?
fs_event_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("c2", "c4"), function(comp) {
  key <- paste0(comp, "_allsamples")
  if (!key %in% names(set_results)) return(NULL)
  fc <- set_results[[key]]$frame_comp
  fw <- set_results[[key]]$frame_walk
  if (is.null(fc) || is.null(fw)) return(NULL)
  ps <- fc$pair_summary
  fw_events <- fw$events
  comp_lbl <- comp_label(comp)

  do.call(rbind, lapply(fs_frame_cats, function(cat) {
    # Get pairs in this frame category
    cat_pairs <- ps[ps$frame_category == cat,
                    c("reference_isoform_id", "comparator_isoform_id")]
    if (nrow(cat_pairs) == 0) return(NULL)

    # Get frameshift-causing events for these pairs
    fs_evts <- fw_events[fw_events$is_frameshift == TRUE, ]
    fs_evts <- merge(fs_evts, cat_pairs,
                     by = c("reference_isoform_id", "comparator_isoform_id"))
    if (nrow(fs_evts) == 0) return(NULL)

    # Count by event type
    evt_counts <- as.data.frame(table(fs_evts$event_type), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    names(evt_counts) <- c("event_type", "n_fs_events")
    evt_counts$pct_of_fs_events <- round(100 * evt_counts$n_fs_events /
                                          sum(evt_counts$n_fs_events), 1)
    evt_counts$frame_category <- cat
    evt_counts$comparison <- comp_lbl
    evt_counts$n_pairs <- nrow(cat_pairs)
    evt_counts[order(-evt_counts$n_fs_events), ]
  }))
}))

if (!is.null(fs_event_rows) && nrow(fs_event_rows) > 0) {
  rownames(fs_event_rows) <- NULL
  knitr::kable(
    fs_event_rows[, c("frame_category", "comparison", "event_type",
                       "n_fs_events", "pct_of_fs_events")],
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption = "Frameshift-Causing Events by Frame Category (all_samples)") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")
}

# --- Stacked bar chart ---
if (!is.null(fs_event_rows) && nrow(fs_event_rows) > 0 && has_ggplot2) {
  fs_cat_labels <- c(
    same_start_frameshift = "Same Start\nFrameshift",
    diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift = "Diff Start\nDiff Frame + FS"
  )
  fs_event_rows$cat_label <- factor(
    fs_cat_labels[fs_event_rows$frame_category],
    levels = fs_cat_labels)

  p_fs_evt <- ggplot(fs_event_rows,
                     aes(x = comparison, y = pct_of_fs_events, fill = event_type)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ cat_label, nrow = 1) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of frameshift-causing events",
         fill = "Event Type",
         title = "Which Splicing Events Cause Frameshifts? (all_samples)",
         subtitle = "Distribution of frameshift-causing event types within each frame category")
  print(p_fs_evt)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Frameshift Consequences

Among pairs that share the same start codon, splicing-induced frameshifts are common in both
NMD and Control comparisons, but their downstream consequences differ sharply. In NMD pairs,
frameshifts overwhelmingly produce PTCs that trigger decay. In Control pairs, most frameshifts
place the new stop codon in the last exon (0 downstream EJCs), producing stable proteins with
rewritten C-terminal sequences — productive alternative splicing generating protein diversity.

### Frameshift Outcome Distribution

Same-start coding pairs are partitioned into four mutually exclusive outcome categories, each
expressed as a percentage of all same-start coding pairs (so bars across categories sum to
100% within each cell type). This uses the cross-isoform reading frame comparison
(`compareIsoformFrames()` in `Isopair/R/ptc.R`; see METHODS.md §Reading Frame and PTC
Analysis). Only pairs classified as `same_start_in_frame` or `same_start_frameshift` are
included, since these share translation initiation and any frame difference is attributable
to splicing.

The four categories are:

- **In Frame**: Same start codon, no frameshift — splicing differences preserve reading frame.
- **Frameshift → PTC**: Frameshift produces a premature stop codon (>50 nt upstream of last
  EJC), triggering NMD.
- **Frameshift → Stop in Last Exon**: Frameshift without PTC; stop codon falls in the last
  exon (0 downstream EJCs), producing a stable protein with novel C-terminal sequence.
- **Frameshift → Other**: Frameshift without PTC and stop not in last exon.

```{r sec5-frameshift-outcome, results='asis', fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
outcome_rows <- compute_frameshift_outcome_rows("all_samples")

if (!is.null(outcome_rows)) {
  outcome_tbl <- outcome_rows
  outcome_tbl$in_frame_pct <- round(100 * outcome_tbl$n_in_frame / outcome_tbl$n_same_start, 1)
  outcome_tbl$fs_ptc_pct <- round(100 * outcome_tbl$n_fs_ptc / outcome_tbl$n_same_start, 1)
  outcome_tbl$fs_stop_last_pct <- round(100 * outcome_tbl$n_fs_stop_last / outcome_tbl$n_same_start, 1)
  outcome_tbl$fs_other_pct <- round(100 * outcome_tbl$n_fs_other / outcome_tbl$n_same_start, 1)
  rownames(outcome_tbl) <- NULL
  knitr::kable(outcome_tbl[, c("cell_type", "comparison", "n_same_start",
                                "n_in_frame", "in_frame_pct",
                                "n_fs_ptc", "fs_ptc_pct",
                                "n_fs_stop_last", "fs_stop_last_pct",
                                "n_fs_other", "fs_other_pct")],
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption = "Frameshift Outcome Distribution: NMD vs Control (Same-Start Pairs, all_samples)") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")
}

# --- Stacked bar chart: outcomes as % of same-start pairs (all_samples only) ---
if (!is.null(outcome_rows) && has_ggplot2) {
  outcome_cats <- c("In Frame", "Frameshift\n\u2192 PTC",
                    "Frameshift\n\u2192 Stop in Last Exon", "Frameshift\n\u2192 Other")

  outcome_plot_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(outcome_rows)), function(i) {
    r <- outcome_rows[i, ]
    n <- r$n_same_start
    data.frame(
      comparison = r$comparison,
      outcome = outcome_cats,
      n = c(r$n_in_frame, r$n_fs_ptc, r$n_fs_stop_last, r$n_fs_other),
      pct = 100 * c(r$n_in_frame, r$n_fs_ptc, r$n_fs_stop_last, r$n_fs_other) / max(n, 1)
    )
  }))
  outcome_plot_df$outcome <- factor(outcome_plot_df$outcome, levels = outcome_cats)

  # Fisher's test per outcome category
  nmd_row <- outcome_rows[outcome_rows$comparison == "NMD", ]
  ctrl_row <- outcome_rows[outcome_rows$comparison == "Control", ]
  p_labels <- NULL
  if (nrow(nmd_row) > 0 && nrow(ctrl_row) > 0) {
    count_cols <- c("n_in_frame", "n_fs_ptc", "n_fs_stop_last", "n_fs_other")
    p_labels <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(outcome_cats), function(j) {
      ft <- tryCatch({
        mat <- matrix(c(nmd_row[[count_cols[j]]], nmd_row$n_same_start - nmd_row[[count_cols[j]]],
                        ctrl_row[[count_cols[j]]], ctrl_row$n_same_start - ctrl_row[[count_cols[j]]]), nrow = 2)
        fisher.test(mat)
      }, error = function(e) list(p.value = NA))
      p <- ft$p.value
      stars <- if (is.na(p)) "" else if (p < 0.001) "***" else if (p < 0.01) "**" else if (p < 0.05) "*" else "ns"
      max_pct <- max(outcome_plot_df$pct[outcome_plot_df$outcome == outcome_cats[j]], na.rm = TRUE)
      data.frame(outcome = outcome_cats[j], p_star = stars, max_pct = max_pct)
    }))
    p_labels$outcome <- factor(p_labels$outcome, levels = outcome_cats)
  }

  p_out <- ggplot(outcome_plot_df, aes(x = comparison, y = pct, fill = comparison)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
    { if (!is.null(p_labels)) geom_text(data = p_labels, aes(x = 1.5, y = max_pct + 4, label = p_star),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, fontface = "bold") } +
    facet_wrap(~ outcome, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("NMD" = "#ef8a62", "Control" = "#67a9cf"), name = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of same-start pairs",
         title = "Frameshift Outcome Distribution: NMD vs Control (all_samples)",
         subtitle = "All categories sum to 100%. Numbers above bars = pair counts. *** p<0.001, ** p<0.01, * p<0.05 (Fisher's exact test)")
  print(p_out)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

In NMD comparisons, splicing-induced frameshifts overwhelmingly produce PTCs that trigger decay.
In Control comparisons, most frameshifts place the new stop codon in the last exon
(0 downstream EJCs), producing a stable mRNA with a novel C-terminal protein sequence.

### Productive Frameshifts (Control)

Control (C4) pairs with same-start splicing-induced frameshifts and no PTC represent productive
alternative splicing: the frameshift rewrites the C-terminal protein sequence without triggering
NMD. These `r nrow(compute_novel_protein("all_samples"))` pairs produce stable mRNAs encoding
proteins with novel C-terminal sequences — a different protein, not a degraded one.

```{r sec5-novel-protein}
# Compute novel protein metrics for C4 same_start_frameshift pairs without PTC
# all_samples for main body; per-CT computed in Section 5
novel_protein_results <- list()
novel_protein_results[["all_samples"]] <- compute_novel_protein("all_samples")
```

**Columns:** **n_stable_novel** = C4 same-start frameshifts without PTC; **pct_of_same_start** = as % of all C4 same-start coding pairs; **median_novel_aa / iqr_novel_aa** = novel amino acids (translated in shifted frame); **median_total_aa** = total protein length; **median_pct_novel / iqr_pct_novel** = % of protein that is novel sequence.

```{r sec5-novel-protein-table, results='asis'}
np_as <- novel_protein_results[["all_samples"]]
novel_summary <- NULL
if (!is.null(np_as) && nrow(np_as) > 0) {
  fc <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$frame_comp
  n_same_start <- sum(fc$pair_summary$frame_category %in%
    c("same_start_in_frame", "same_start_frameshift"))
  novel_summary <- data.frame(
    n_stable_novel = nrow(np_as),
    pct_of_same_start = round(100 * nrow(np_as) / n_same_start, 1),
    median_novel_aa = round(median(np_as$novel_aa), 0),
    iqr_novel_aa = paste0(round(quantile(np_as$novel_aa, 0.25), 0), "-",
                          round(quantile(np_as$novel_aa, 0.75), 0)),
    median_total_aa = round(median(np_as$total_aa), 0),
    median_pct_novel = round(median(np_as$pct_novel), 1),
    iqr_pct_novel = paste0(round(quantile(np_as$pct_novel, 0.25), 1), "-",
                           round(quantile(np_as$pct_novel, 0.75), 1))
  )
  knitr::kable(novel_summary, caption = "Stable Novel Proteins: Control (C4) Same-Start Frameshifts Without PTC (all_samples)") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

```{r sec5-novel-protein-plot, fig.height=5}
if (has_ggplot2 && !is.null(np_as) && nrow(np_as) > 0) {
  p_novel <- ggplot(data.frame(pct_novel = np_as$pct_novel), aes(x = pct_novel)) +
    geom_density(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = "Novel Protein Sequence in Stable Control Frameshifts (all_samples)",
         subtitle = "C4 unresolved frameshifts without PTC — % of protein in shifted reading frame",
         x = "% of protein that is novel sequence", y = "Density")
  print(p_novel)
}
```

```{r sec5-pf-load-cache}
# Load pre-computed productive frameshift characterization
pf_cache_path <- file.path(data_dir, "analysis_cache", "productive_frameshift_allsamples.rds")
pf_data <- if (file.exists(pf_cache_path)) readRDS(pf_cache_path) else NULL
has_pf <- !is.null(pf_data)
if (has_pf) {
  pf_char <- pf_data$characterization
  pf_ms   <- pf_data$massspec
  pf_dom  <- pf_data$domains
  pf_cons <- pf_data$conservation
}
```

#### Frameshift Mechanisms

Splicing events that cause productive frameshifts — which event types shift reading frame
without introducing a PTC?

```{r sec5-pf-mechanisms, results='asis', fig.height=5}
if (has_pf && has_ggplot2) {
  # Expand comma-separated event types to one row per event type per pair
  event_types_raw <- pf_char$frameshift_event_types[!is.na(pf_char$frameshift_event_types)]
  all_event_types <- unlist(strsplit(event_types_raw, ","))
  event_freq <- sort(table(all_event_types), decreasing = TRUE)

  event_df <- data.frame(
    event_type = names(event_freq),
    count = as.integer(event_freq),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  event_df$pct <- round(100 * event_df$count / length(event_types_raw), 1)

  knitr::kable(event_df,
    col.names = c("Event Type", "Pairs", "% of Pairs"),
    caption = "Splicing events causing productive frameshifts (a pair may have >1 event type)") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")

  # Bar chart
  p_evt <- ggplot(event_df, aes(x = reorder(event_type, -count), y = count)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    labs(x = "Splicing Event Type", y = "Number of Pairs",
         title = "Frameshift-Causing Event Types in Productive Frameshifts")
  print(p_evt)

  # Scatter: pct_novel vs total protein length
  pf_plot <- pf_char[!is.na(pf_char$frameshift_event_types), ]
  # Use primary (first) event type for coloring
  pf_plot$primary_event <- sapply(strsplit(pf_plot$frameshift_event_types, ","), `[`, 1)

  p_scatter <- ggplot(pf_plot, aes(x = total_aa, y = pct_novel, color = primary_event)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2.5) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    labs(x = "Total Protein Length (aa)", y = "% Novel Sequence",
         color = "Primary Event",
         title = "Novel Protein Fraction vs Protein Size",
         subtitle = "Colored by primary frameshift-causing event type")
  print(p_scatter)
}
```

#### Functional Domain Impact

Domain annotations from Pfam/InterPro for ENST isoforms, classified relative to the frameshift
boundary: **conserved** (entirely upstream), **disrupted** (spanning the boundary), or
**novel_region** (entirely downstream, in the frameshifted sequence). For novel isoforms
without Ensembl IDs, conserved-region domains are proxied from the paired ENST isoform
(marked as "ref proxy" in the domain source column).

```{r sec5-pf-domains, results='asis', fig.height=5}
if (has_pf && nrow(pf_dom) > 0 && has_ggplot2) {
  # Per-pair summary: does this pair have any disrupted domains?
  pair_domain_summary <- pf_dom |>
    (\(d) {
      pairs_with_disrupted <- unique(d$gene_id[d$position_class == "disrupted"])
      pairs_with_any <- unique(d$gene_id)
      all_pairs <- unique(pf_char$gene_id)

      data.frame(
        category = c("At least one domain disrupted",
                      "Domains only in conserved region",
                      "No annotated domains"),
        n_pairs = c(
          length(pairs_with_disrupted),
          length(setdiff(pairs_with_any, pairs_with_disrupted)),
          length(setdiff(all_pairs, pairs_with_any))
        )
      )
    })()
  pair_domain_summary$pct <- round(100 * pair_domain_summary$n_pairs /
                                     nrow(pf_char), 1)

  knitr::kable(pair_domain_summary,
    col.names = c("Category", "N Pairs", "% of Total"),
    caption = "Domain disposition across productive frameshift pairs") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")

  # Stacked bar: position class distribution
  pos_freq <- as.data.frame(table(pf_dom$position_class))
  names(pos_freq) <- c("position", "count")
  pos_freq$position <- factor(pos_freq$position,
                                levels = c("conserved", "disrupted", "novel_region"))

  p_dom_bar <- ggplot(pos_freq, aes(x = position, y = count, fill = position)) +
    geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(conserved = "grey60", disrupted = "tomato",
                                  novel_region = "steelblue")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(x = "Domain Position Relative to Frameshift",
         y = "Number of Domain Annotations",
         title = "Functional Domain Disposition in Productive Frameshifts")
  print(p_dom_bar)

  # DT table: per-pair domain details
  dom_display <- pf_dom[, c("gene_id", "isoform_id", "isoform_role",
                              "domain_id", "domain_name", "domain_source",
                              "domain_start_aa", "domain_end_aa", "position_class")]
  dom_display$gene_symbol <- gene_symbol_lookup[dom_display$gene_id]
  dom_display <- dom_display[, c("gene_symbol", "gene_id", "isoform_id", "isoform_role",
                                   "domain_id", "domain_name", "domain_source",
                                   "domain_start_aa", "domain_end_aa", "position_class")]
  render_dt(dom_display,
    caption = "Domain annotations for productive frameshift isoforms (filterable)")
} else if (has_pf) {
  cat("No domain annotations were retrieved (biomaRt may have been unavailable).\n\n")
}
```

#### Proteomics Evidence

Mass-spectrometry evidence from the EBI Proteomics database for peptides unique to the
novel C-terminal region. Peptides are generated via in-silico tryptic digest (7-30 aa,
cleaving at K/R not followed by P) and filtered to those absent from the reference protein.

```{r sec5-pf-massspec, results='asis'}
if (has_pf && nrow(pf_ms) > 0) {
  n_queried_genes <- length(unique(pf_ms$comparator_isoform_id))
  n_hit_genes <- length(unique(pf_ms$comparator_isoform_id[pf_ms$ebi_hit]))
  n_gene_match <- length(unique(pf_ms$comparator_isoform_id[pf_ms$ebi_gene_match]))

  ms_summary <- data.frame(
    metric = c("Genes queried (with unique peptides)",
               "Genes with any EBI hit",
               "Genes with gene-matched hit",
               "Total unique peptides queried",
               "Peptides with EBI hits"),
    value = c(n_queried_genes, n_hit_genes, n_gene_match,
              nrow(pf_ms), sum(pf_ms$ebi_hit))
  )
  knitr::kable(ms_summary, col.names = c("Metric", "N"),
    caption = "Mass-spectrometry evidence for novel-region peptides") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")

  # Show hits if any
  ms_hits <- pf_ms[pf_ms$ebi_hit, ]
  if (nrow(ms_hits) > 0) {
    ms_hits$gene_symbol <- gene_symbol_lookup[ms_hits$gene_id]
    hit_display <- ms_hits[, c("gene_symbol", "gene_id", "comparator_isoform_id",
                                 "peptide", "peptide_length", "ebi_gene_match",
                                 "ebi_accession")]
    render_dt(hit_display, caption = "Peptides with EBI proteomics evidence")
  }
} else if (has_pf) {
  cat("No mass-spec queries were performed (no novel-region peptides met length criteria).\n\n")
}
```

Most productive frameshifts lack mass-spec evidence for their novel C-terminal peptides.
This is expected: (1) these are minor isoforms with lower expression; (2) the novel
regions are short (median ~40 aa), limiting the number of tryptic peptides; (3) proteomics
databases are biased toward principal isoforms. The few genes with hits typically correspond
to known alternative isoforms whose "novel" sequence is only novel relative to the dominant
isoform in the pair, not globally unknown.

#### Isoform Annotation Status

APPRIS, TSL (Transcript Support Level), and UniProt annotations for reference and comparator
isoforms. This reveals whether productive frameshifts involve well-characterized alternative
isoforms or poorly annotated transcripts.

```{r sec5-pf-conservation, results='asis'}
if (has_pf) {
  # APPRIS breakdown
  ref_appris <- table(pf_cons$ref_appris, useNA = "ifany")
  comp_appris <- table(pf_cons$comp_appris, useNA = "ifany")

  appris_df <- merge(
    data.frame(appris = names(ref_appris), reference = as.integer(ref_appris)),
    data.frame(appris = names(comp_appris), comparator = as.integer(comp_appris)),
    by = "appris", all = TRUE
  )
  appris_df$appris[is.na(appris_df$appris)] <- "(no annotation)"
  appris_df$reference[is.na(appris_df$reference)] <- 0
  appris_df$comparator[is.na(appris_df$comparator)] <- 0

  knitr::kable(appris_df, col.names = c("APPRIS", "Reference", "Comparator"),
    caption = "APPRIS classification: reference vs comparator isoforms") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")

  # TSL breakdown for comparators
  comp_tsl <- table(pf_cons$comp_tsl, useNA = "ifany")
  tsl_df <- data.frame(tsl = names(comp_tsl), count = as.integer(comp_tsl))
  tsl_df$tsl[is.na(tsl_df$tsl)] <- "(novel/no annotation)"
  knitr::kable(tsl_df, col.names = c("TSL", "Comparator Count"),
    caption = "Transcript Support Level for comparator (frameshifted) isoforms") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")

  # UniProt for ENST comparators
  enst_cons <- pf_cons[grepl("^ENST", pf_cons$comparator_isoform_id), ]
  if (any(!is.na(enst_cons$comp_uniprot_accession))) {
    uniprot_summary <- data.frame(
      category = c("Swiss-Prot (reviewed)", "TrEMBL (unreviewed)", "No UniProt entry"),
      count = c(
        sum(enst_cons$comp_uniprot_reviewed == "Swiss-Prot", na.rm = TRUE),
        sum(enst_cons$comp_uniprot_reviewed == "TrEMBL", na.rm = TRUE),
        sum(is.na(enst_cons$comp_uniprot_accession))
      )
    )
    knitr::kable(uniprot_summary, col.names = c("UniProt Status", "ENST Comparators"),
      caption = "UniProt protein existence for ENST comparator isoforms") |> print()
    cat("\n\n")

    # Show Swiss-Prot entries
    swissprot <- enst_cons[!is.na(enst_cons$comp_uniprot_reviewed) &
                             enst_cons$comp_uniprot_reviewed == "Swiss-Prot", ]
    if (nrow(swissprot) > 0) {
      swissprot$gene_symbol <- gene_symbol_lookup[swissprot$gene_id]
      sp_display <- swissprot[, c("gene_symbol", "comparator_isoform_id",
                                    "comp_uniprot_accession", "comp_protein_existence",
                                    "comp_appris", "comp_tsl")]
      render_dt(sp_display,
        caption = "ENST comparators with Swiss-Prot (reviewed) entries")
    }
  }
}
```

Productive frameshifts predominantly involve alternative (non-principal) isoforms as the
comparator. The reference (dominant) isoform is typically the APPRIS principal isoform,
while the frameshifted comparator is an alternative isoform — consistent with the
biological expectation that productive frameshifts represent regulated alternative splicing
producing functionally distinct protein variants.

### Frameshift Examples: Real Gene Cases

Four real gene examples illustrating the major categories of reading frame outcomes.
Panel A: a same-start splicing-induced frameshift that produces a PTC, triggering NMD.
Panel B: a different-start, different-frame isoform without PTC, producing a stable protein
with novel C-terminal sequence.
Panel C: a different-start, different-frame isoform with PTC, triggering NMD.
Panel D: a canonical poison exon — same start codon, in frame, but an included or retained
exonic region introduces a premature stop codon.

Each example is shown first as a full-gene overview, then zoomed to the region containing
the key splicing event.

```{r sec5-frameshift-examples, fig.width=12, fig.height=24}
if (has_ggplot2) {
  # Helper: resolve gene symbol from gene_id
  get_gene_sym <- function(gid) {
    sym <- gene_symbol_lookup[gid]
    if (is.na(sym) || sym == "") gid else sym
  }

  # Helper: zoom on a SPECIFIC subset of events (e.g., the frameshift-causing one)
  compute_event_zoom <- function(events, padding_frac = 0.3) {
    if (is.null(events) || nrow(events) == 0) return(NULL)
    ev_min <- min(events$five_prime, events$three_prime, na.rm = TRUE)
    ev_max <- max(events$five_prime, events$three_prime, na.rm = TRUE)
    span <- ev_max - ev_min
    pad <- max(span * padding_frac, 500)
    c(ev_min - pad, ev_max + pad)
  }

  # Helper: find frameshift-causing events using frame_walk
  # Returns data frame with five_prime/three_prime columns for compute_event_zoom()
  get_fs_events <- function(fw, ref_id, comp_id) {
    if (is.null(fw) || is.null(fw$events) || nrow(fw$events) == 0) return(NULL)
    fs <- fw$events[fw$events$reference_isoform_id == ref_id &
                    fw$events$comparator_isoform_id == comp_id &
                    fw$events$is_frameshift == TRUE, ]
    if (nrow(fs) == 0) return(NULL)
    # Return with five_prime/three_prime names for compute_event_zoom()
    data.frame(five_prime = fs$genomic_start, three_prime = fs$genomic_end)
  }

  # Helper: build a plot pair (full + zoom) and append to plot list
  build_panel <- function(pick, prof_key, ref_label, comp_label_text,
                          title_text, sub_text, annotations = list(),
                          zoom_events = NULL) {
    ref_ex <- get_exon_coords(pick$reference_isoform_id, structures)
    comp_ex <- get_exon_coords(pick$comparator_isoform_id, structures)
    ref_cds_r <- get_cds_range(pick$reference_isoform_id, cds)
    comp_cds_r <- get_cds_range(pick$comparator_isoform_id, cds)
    str_row <- structures[structures$isoform_id == pick$reference_isoform_id, ]
    gene_strand <- str_row$strand[1]

    profs <- set_results[[prof_key]]$profiles
    pair_prof <- profs[profs$reference_isoform_id == pick$reference_isoform_id &
                       profs$comparator_isoform_id == pick$comparator_isoform_id, ]
    pair_events <- if (nrow(pair_prof) > 0) pair_prof$detailed_events[[1]] else NULL

    plots <- list()
    plots[["full"]] <- plot_ucsc_pair(
      ref_ex$starts, ref_ex$ends, comp_ex$starts, comp_ex$ends, gene_strand,
      ref_cds = ref_cds_r, comp_cds = comp_cds_r,
      ref_label = ref_label, comp_label = comp_label_text,
      events = pair_events, annotations = annotations,
      title = title_text, subtitle = sub_text
    )

    # Zoom: use zoom_events if provided, otherwise all events
    zoom_target <- if (!is.null(zoom_events) && nrow(zoom_events) > 0) zoom_events else pair_events
    zoom_lim <- compute_event_zoom(zoom_target)
    if (!is.null(zoom_lim)) {
      plots[["zoom"]] <- plot_ucsc_pair(
        ref_ex$starts, ref_ex$ends, comp_ex$starts, comp_ex$ends, gene_strand,
        ref_cds = ref_cds_r, comp_cds = comp_cds_r,
        ref_label = ref_label, comp_label = comp_label_text,
        events = pair_events, annotations = annotations,
        title = paste0(title_text, " [ZOOM]"), subtitle = sub_text,
        xlim = zoom_lim
      )
    }
    list(plots = plots, strand = gene_strand, ref_cds = ref_cds_r, comp_cds = comp_cds_r)
  }

  # Use all_samples pooled data (matching main body)
  c2_key <- "c2_allsamples"
  c4_key <- "c4_allsamples"
  fc_c2 <- set_results[[c2_key]]$frame_comp
  fc_c4 <- set_results[[c4_key]]$frame_comp
  fw_c2 <- set_results[[c2_key]]$frame_walk
  fw_c4 <- set_results[[c4_key]]$frame_walk

  example_plots <- list()

  # --- Panel A: Same-start frameshift → PTC (NMD, C2) ---
  if (!is.null(fc_c2)) {
    ps_c2 <- fc_c2$pair_summary
    fs_c2 <- ps_c2[ps_c2$frame_category == "same_start_frameshift", ]
    fs_c2_ptc <- merge(fs_c2, ptc[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE, c("isoform_id", "has_ptc",
                       "ptc_distance", "n_downstream_ejcs")],
                       by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    fs_c2_ptc <- merge(fs_c2_ptc,
                       structures[, c("isoform_id", "n_exons")],
                       by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    names(fs_c2_ptc)[names(fs_c2_ptc) == "n_exons"] <- "comp_n_exons"
    fs_c2_ptc <- merge(fs_c2_ptc,
                       structures[, c("isoform_id", "n_exons")],
                       by.x = "reference_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    names(fs_c2_ptc)[names(fs_c2_ptc) == "n_exons"] <- "ref_n_exons"
    fs_c2_ptc$exon_diff <- abs(fs_c2_ptc$ref_n_exons - fs_c2_ptc$comp_n_exons)
    candidates_a <- fs_c2_ptc[fs_c2_ptc$comp_n_exons >= 3 & fs_c2_ptc$comp_n_exons <= 10 &
                               fs_c2_ptc$exon_diff <= 1, ]
    if (nrow(candidates_a) > 0) {
      pick_a <- candidates_a[which.max(candidates_a$ptc_distance), ]

      # Find the frameshift-causing event for targeted zoom
      fs_evts_a <- get_fs_events(fw_c2, pick_a$reference_isoform_id,
                                  pick_a$comparator_isoform_id)

      # PTC annotation
      str_row_a <- structures[structures$isoform_id == pick_a$reference_isoform_id, ]
      strand_a <- str_row_a$strand[1]
      comp_cds_a <- get_cds_range(pick_a$comparator_isoform_id, cds)
      ptc_ann <- list()
      if (!is.null(comp_cds_a)) {
        ptc_pos <- if (strand_a == "+") comp_cds_a$cds_stop else comp_cds_a$cds_start
        ptc_ann <- list(
          list(type = "ptc_marker", x = ptc_pos, track = "comp",
               label = "PTC", color = "#E74C3C")
        )
      }

      gene_sym_a <- get_gene_sym(pick_a$gene_id)
      title_a <- sprintf("A) Same-Start Frameshift \u2192 PTC: %s (%s)",
                         gene_sym_a, pick_a$gene_id)
      sub_a <- sprintf("Ref: %s | Comp: %s\nPTC distance = %d nt, %d downstream EJC(s)",
                       pick_a$reference_isoform_id, pick_a$comparator_isoform_id,
                       round(pick_a$ptc_distance), pick_a$n_downstream_ejcs)

      # Zoom spans from frameshift-causing event to PTC position
      zoom_df_a <- fs_evts_a
      if (!is.null(zoom_df_a) && !is.null(comp_cds_a)) {
        ptc_pos_a <- if (strand_a == "+") comp_cds_a$cds_stop else comp_cds_a$cds_start
        zoom_df_a <- rbind(zoom_df_a,
                           data.frame(five_prime = ptc_pos_a, three_prime = ptc_pos_a))
      }

      panel_a <- build_panel(pick_a, c2_key, "Dominant\n(non-NMD)", "NMD-sensitive",
                             title_a, sub_a, annotations = ptc_ann,
                             zoom_events = zoom_df_a)
      example_plots <- c(example_plots, panel_a$plots)
    }
  }

  # --- Panel B: Diff-start diff-frame → Novel Protein (no PTC, C2) ---
  if (!is.null(fc_c2)) {
    ps_c2 <- fc_c2$pair_summary
    ds_c2 <- ps_c2[ps_c2$frame_category %in% c("diff_start_diff_frame",
                    "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift"), ]
    # Exclude PTC+ comparators
    ds_c2_noptc <- merge(ds_c2, ptc[, c("isoform_id", "has_ptc")],
                         by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id", all.x = TRUE)
    ds_c2_noptc <- ds_c2_noptc[is.na(ds_c2_noptc$has_ptc) | ds_c2_noptc$has_ptc == FALSE, ]
    # Require coding comparator (has CDS)
    ds_c2_noptc <- ds_c2_noptc[ds_c2_noptc$comparator_isoform_id %in% cds$isoform_id, ]
    ds_c2_noptc <- merge(ds_c2_noptc,
                         structures[, c("isoform_id", "n_exons")],
                         by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    candidates_b <- ds_c2_noptc[ds_c2_noptc$n_exons >= 3 & ds_c2_noptc$n_exons <= 10, ]
    # Prefer pairs with moderate frameshifted CDS for visual interest
    if (nrow(candidates_b) > 0) {
      candidates_b <- candidates_b[candidates_b$pct_shared_cds_frameshifted >= 30 &
                                    candidates_b$pct_shared_cds_frameshifted <= 80, ]
    }
    if (nrow(candidates_b) > 0) {
      pick_b <- candidates_b[1, ]

      # Annotation: different start codons
      ref_cds_b <- get_cds_range(pick_b$reference_isoform_id, cds)
      comp_cds_b <- get_cds_range(pick_b$comparator_isoform_id, cds)
      str_row_b <- structures[structures$isoform_id == pick_b$reference_isoform_id, ]
      strand_b <- str_row_b$strand[1]

      ds_ann <- list()
      if (!is.null(ref_cds_b) && !is.null(comp_cds_b)) {
        ref_start_pos <- if (strand_b == "+") ref_cds_b$cds_start else ref_cds_b$cds_stop
        comp_start_pos <- if (strand_b == "+") comp_cds_b$cds_start else comp_cds_b$cds_stop
        ds_ann <- list(
          list(type = "ptc_marker", x = ref_start_pos, track = "ref",
               label = "ATG", color = "#27AE60"),
          list(type = "ptc_marker", x = comp_start_pos, track = "comp",
               label = "ATG", color = "#27AE60")
        )
      }

      gene_sym_b <- get_gene_sym(pick_b$gene_id)
      title_b <- sprintf("B) Diff-Start Diff-Frame \u2192 Novel Protein: %s (%s)",
                         gene_sym_b, pick_b$gene_id)
      sub_b <- sprintf("Ref: %s | Comp: %s\nDifferent start codons, %.0f%% of shared CDS frameshifted, no PTC",
                       pick_b$reference_isoform_id, pick_b$comparator_isoform_id,
                       pick_b$pct_shared_cds_frameshifted)

      panel_b <- build_panel(pick_b, c2_key, "Dominant\n(non-NMD)", "NMD-sensitive",
                             title_b, sub_b, annotations = ds_ann,
                             zoom_events = NULL)
      example_plots <- c(example_plots, panel_b$plots)
    }
  }

  # --- Panel C: Diff-start diff-frame → PTC (NMD, C2) ---
  if (!is.null(fc_c2)) {
    ps_c2 <- fc_c2$pair_summary
    ds_c2 <- ps_c2[ps_c2$frame_category %in% c("diff_start_diff_frame",
                    "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift"), ]
    ds_c2_ptc <- merge(ds_c2, ptc[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE, c("isoform_id", "has_ptc",
                       "ptc_distance", "n_downstream_ejcs")],
                       by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    ds_c2_ptc <- merge(ds_c2_ptc,
                       structures[, c("isoform_id", "n_exons")],
                       by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    names(ds_c2_ptc)[names(ds_c2_ptc) == "n_exons"] <- "comp_n_exons"
    candidates_c <- ds_c2_ptc[ds_c2_ptc$comp_n_exons >= 3 & ds_c2_ptc$comp_n_exons <= 10, ]
    if (nrow(candidates_c) > 0) {
      pick_c <- candidates_c[which.max(candidates_c$ptc_distance), ]

      str_row_c <- structures[structures$isoform_id == pick_c$reference_isoform_id, ]
      strand_c <- str_row_c$strand[1]
      comp_cds_c <- get_cds_range(pick_c$comparator_isoform_id, cds)
      ref_cds_c <- get_cds_range(pick_c$reference_isoform_id, cds)

      # Annotations: different start codons + PTC
      ptc_ds_ann <- list()
      if (!is.null(ref_cds_c) && !is.null(comp_cds_c)) {
        ref_start_pos <- if (strand_c == "+") ref_cds_c$cds_start else ref_cds_c$cds_stop
        comp_start_pos <- if (strand_c == "+") comp_cds_c$cds_start else comp_cds_c$cds_stop
        ptc_pos_c <- if (strand_c == "+") comp_cds_c$cds_stop else comp_cds_c$cds_start
        ptc_ds_ann <- list(
          list(type = "ptc_marker", x = ref_start_pos, track = "ref",
               label = "ATG", color = "#27AE60"),
          list(type = "ptc_marker", x = comp_start_pos, track = "comp",
               label = "ATG", color = "#27AE60"),
          list(type = "ptc_marker", x = ptc_pos_c, track = "comp",
               label = "PTC", color = "#E74C3C")
        )
      }

      gene_sym_c <- get_gene_sym(pick_c$gene_id)
      title_c <- sprintf("C) Diff-Start Diff-Frame \u2192 PTC: %s (%s)",
                         gene_sym_c, pick_c$gene_id)
      sub_c <- sprintf("Ref: %s | Comp: %s\nDifferent start codons, PTC distance = %d nt, %d downstream EJC(s)",
                       pick_c$reference_isoform_id, pick_c$comparator_isoform_id,
                       round(pick_c$ptc_distance), pick_c$n_downstream_ejcs)

      # Zoom on the PTC region
      zoom_df_c <- NULL
      if (!is.null(comp_cds_c)) {
        ptc_pos_c <- if (strand_c == "+") comp_cds_c$cds_stop else comp_cds_c$cds_start
        zoom_df_c <- data.frame(five_prime = ptc_pos_c, three_prime = ptc_pos_c)
      }

      panel_c <- build_panel(pick_c, c2_key, "Dominant\n(non-NMD)", "NMD-sensitive",
                             title_c, sub_c, annotations = ptc_ds_ann,
                             zoom_events = zoom_df_c)
      example_plots <- c(example_plots, panel_c$plots)
    }
  }

  # --- Panel D: Canonical Poison Exon (same start, in frame, PTC from included exon) ---
  if (!is.null(fc_c2)) {
    ps_c2 <- fc_c2$pair_summary
    sif_c2 <- ps_c2[ps_c2$frame_category == "same_start_in_frame", ]
    # Find in-frame pairs where the comparator has a PTC
    sif_c2_ptc <- merge(sif_c2, ptc[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE, c("isoform_id", "has_ptc",
                        "ptc_distance", "n_downstream_ejcs")],
                        by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    # Merge exon counts
    sif_c2_ptc <- merge(sif_c2_ptc,
                        structures[, c("isoform_id", "n_exons")],
                        by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    names(sif_c2_ptc)[names(sif_c2_ptc) == "n_exons"] <- "comp_n_exons"
    sif_c2_ptc <- merge(sif_c2_ptc,
                        structures[, c("isoform_id", "n_exons")],
                        by.x = "reference_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id")
    names(sif_c2_ptc)[names(sif_c2_ptc) == "n_exons"] <- "ref_n_exons"
    # Prefer cases where comparator has MORE exons (included exon) or same (retained intron)
    candidates_d <- sif_c2_ptc[sif_c2_ptc$comp_n_exons >= 3 &
                                sif_c2_ptc$comp_n_exons <= 12, ]
    if (nrow(candidates_d) > 0) {
      # Prefer high ptc_distance and multiple downstream EJCs for clear NMD
      candidates_d <- candidates_d[order(-candidates_d$n_downstream_ejcs,
                                          -candidates_d$ptc_distance), ]
      pick_d <- candidates_d[1, ]

      str_row_d <- structures[structures$isoform_id == pick_d$reference_isoform_id, ]
      strand_d <- str_row_d$strand[1]
      comp_cds_d <- get_cds_range(pick_d$comparator_isoform_id, cds)

      # PTC annotation
      ptc_pe_ann <- list()
      if (!is.null(comp_cds_d)) {
        ptc_pos_d <- if (strand_d == "+") comp_cds_d$cds_stop else comp_cds_d$cds_start
        ptc_pe_ann <- list(
          list(type = "ptc_marker", x = ptc_pos_d, track = "comp",
               label = "PTC", color = "#E74C3C")
        )
      }

      # Identify the event that introduces the PTC (SE, IR, etc.)
      profs_d <- set_results[[c2_key]]$profiles
      pair_prof_d <- profs_d[profs_d$reference_isoform_id == pick_d$reference_isoform_id &
                              profs_d$comparator_isoform_id == pick_d$comparator_isoform_id, ]
      pair_events_d <- if (nrow(pair_prof_d) > 0) pair_prof_d$detailed_events[[1]] else NULL

      # For zoom: find events closest to PTC position
      zoom_df_d <- NULL
      if (!is.null(pair_events_d) && nrow(pair_events_d) > 0 && !is.null(comp_cds_d)) {
        ptc_pos_d <- if (strand_d == "+") comp_cds_d$cds_stop else comp_cds_d$cds_start
        # Find events that overlap or are near the PTC
        ev_midpoints <- (pmin(pair_events_d$five_prime, pair_events_d$three_prime) +
                         pmax(pair_events_d$five_prime, pair_events_d$three_prime)) / 2
        nearest_idx <- which.min(abs(ev_midpoints - ptc_pos_d))
        nearest_ev <- pair_events_d[nearest_idx, , drop = FALSE]
        # Include PTC position in zoom range
        zoom_df_d <- data.frame(
          five_prime = c(pmin(nearest_ev$five_prime, nearest_ev$three_prime), ptc_pos_d),
          three_prime = c(pmax(nearest_ev$five_prime, nearest_ev$three_prime), ptc_pos_d)
        )
      }

      exon_diff_d <- pick_d$comp_n_exons - pick_d$ref_n_exons
      exon_note <- if (exon_diff_d > 0) {
        sprintf("comparator has %d extra exon(s)", exon_diff_d)
      } else if (exon_diff_d == 0) {
        "same exon count (retained intron or boundary change)"
      } else {
        sprintf("comparator has %d fewer exon(s)", abs(exon_diff_d))
      }

      gene_sym_d <- get_gene_sym(pick_d$gene_id)
      title_d <- sprintf("D) Poison Exon (In-Frame PTC): %s (%s)",
                         gene_sym_d, pick_d$gene_id)
      sub_d <- sprintf("Ref: %s | Comp: %s\nSame start, in frame, %s\nPTC distance = %d nt, %d downstream EJC(s)",
                       pick_d$reference_isoform_id, pick_d$comparator_isoform_id,
                       exon_note,
                       round(pick_d$ptc_distance), pick_d$n_downstream_ejcs)

      panel_d <- build_panel(pick_d, c2_key, "Dominant\n(non-NMD)", "NMD-sensitive",
                             title_d, sub_d, annotations = ptc_pe_ann,
                             zoom_events = zoom_df_d)
      example_plots <- c(example_plots, panel_d$plots)
    }
  }

  # Combine panels: full + zoom pairs
  if (length(example_plots) > 0) {
    if (requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) {
      combined <- patchwork::wrap_plots(example_plots, ncol = 1) +
        patchwork::plot_annotation(
          title = "Reading Frame Consequences: Representative Gene Examples",
          theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))
        )
      print(combined)
    } else {
      for (pp in example_plots) print(pp)
    }
  }
}
```

## Stop Codon Distance to Last EJC

The distance from a transcript's stop codon to the last exon-exon junction (EJC) is a
key determinant of NMD susceptibility. When a stop codon sits >50 nt upstream of the last
EJC, the downstream junction(s) remain associated with the exon junction complex after
splicing, triggering NMD surveillance. Greater distance (more downstream EJCs) is generally
associated with more efficient NMD.

The distance is computed in mRNA coordinates as `last_EJC_position - stop_codon_position`.
Positive values indicate the stop codon is upstream of the last EJC (potential NMD trigger);
negative values indicate a stop codon downstream of the last EJC (normal termination).
Single-exon isoforms have no EJC and are excluded.

### Distribution of Stop-to-EJC Distance: All Comparators

Distribution of stop codon-to-last-EJC distances for **all** comparator isoforms (not just
PTC+), stratified by NMD and Control. This shows the full landscape of stop codon positioning
rather than conditioning on the PTC+ tail.

```{r sec5-stop-dist, results='asis', fig.height=6}
# Build stop-to-EJC distance data for all comparator isoforms — all_samples only
stop_dist_all <- {
  rows <- list()
  for (comp in c("c2", "c4")) {
    key <- paste0(comp, "_allsamples")
    if (!key %in% names(set_results)) next
    comp_ids <- set_results[[key]]$profiles$comparator_isoform_id
    ptc_sub <- ptc[ptc$isoform_id %in% comp_ids & !is.na(ptc$ptc_distance), ]
    if (nrow(ptc_sub) == 0) next
    rows[[comp]] <- data.frame(
      comparison = comp_label(comp),
      ptc_distance = ptc_sub$ptc_distance,
      has_ptc = ptc_sub$has_ptc
    )
  }
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

if (!is.null(stop_dist_all) && nrow(stop_dist_all) > 0 && has_ggplot2) {
  dist_summary <- stop_dist_all |>
    group_by(comparison) |>
    summarize(
      n_isoforms = n(),
      median_dist = round(median(ptc_distance), 0),
      pct_ptc_pos = round(100 * mean(has_ptc), 1),
      pct_negative = round(100 * mean(ptc_distance < 0), 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  cat("**Columns:** **n_isoforms** = comparator isoforms with stop-to-EJC distance computed; ")
  cat("**median_dist** = median distance (nt); **pct_ptc_pos** = % with PTC (distance > 50 nt); ")
  cat("**pct_negative** = % with stop codon downstream of last EJC (normal termination).\n\n")
  knitr::kable(dist_summary, caption = "Stop Codon-to-Last EJC Distance: All Comparators (all_samples)") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")

  p_dist <- ggplot(stop_dist_all, aes(x = ptc_distance, fill = comparison)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = Inf, label = "PTC threshold (50 nt)",
             hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "red") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(
      quantile(stop_dist_all$ptc_distance, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
      quantile(stop_dist_all$ptc_distance, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = "Stop Codon Distance to Last EJC: NMD vs Control Comparators (all_samples)",
         subtitle = "All comparator isoforms (coding, multi-exon). Dashed red = 50 nt PTC threshold.",
         x = "Distance from stop codon to last EJC (nt)", y = "Density", fill = "")
  print(p_dist)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### NMD Response vs Stop Codon Distance (Meta-Analysis Average)

Among NMD-sensitive comparator isoforms, is there a relationship between the distance from
the stop codon to the last EJC and the magnitude of upregulation upon NMD inhibition? Rather
than showing per-cell-type scatter plots, this analysis uses the **mashr meta-analysis**
posterior mean averaged across 5 conditions (DD, AT, DO_ALI, FB, MV; DD_ALI excluded) to
produce a single consensus NMD response estimate per isoform. This leverages cross-condition
borrowing of information for more stable effect-size estimates.

```{r sec5-mashr-load, include=FALSE}
# Load mashr model for meta-analysis logFC
mashr_model_path <- "/Users/petecastaldi/claude_projects/nmd/isocall_dge/mashr/mashr_isoform_model_2026.3.10.rds"
mashr_model <- readRDS(mashr_model_path)

# Extract PosteriorMean matrix (isoforms x conditions)
post_mean <- ashr::get_pm(mashr_model)

# Average across 5 main conditions (exclude DD_ALI = Smg1i_in_DD_ALI)
meta_cols <- c("Smg1i_in_DD", "Smg1i_in_AT", "Smg1i_in_DO_ALI",
               "Smg1i_in_FB", "Smg1i_in_MV")
meta_logfc <- data.frame(
  txid = rownames(post_mean),
  mean_logFC = rowMeans(post_mean[, meta_cols, drop = FALSE])
)
```

```{r sec5-nmd-logfc-dist, results='asis', fig.height=6}
# Get all_samples NMD comparator isoform IDs
comp_ids_as <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles$comparator_isoform_id

# Merge meta-analysis logFC with PTC distance for all_samples comparators
ptc_sub <- ptc[ptc$isoform_id %in% comp_ids_as & !is.na(ptc$ptc_distance),
                c("isoform_id", "ptc_distance", "has_ptc")]
nmd_logfc_dist <- merge(meta_logfc[meta_logfc$txid %in% comp_ids_as, ],
                         ptc_sub, by.x = "txid", by.y = "isoform_id")

if (nrow(nmd_logfc_dist) > 0 && has_ggplot2) {
  p_logfc <- ggplot(nmd_logfc_dist, aes(x = ptc_distance, y = mean_logFC)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "steelblue") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(
      quantile(nmd_logfc_dist$ptc_distance, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
      quantile(nmd_logfc_dist$ptc_distance, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = sprintf("NMD Response vs Stop Codon Distance (all_samples, n = %d)",
                         nrow(nmd_logfc_dist)),
         subtitle = "Meta-analysis average (mashr PosteriorMean across DD, AT, DO_ALI, FB, MV). Blue = loess. Red = 50 nt PTC threshold.",
         x = "Distance from stop codon to last EJC (nt)",
         y = "Mean logFC (mashr, 5 conditions)")
  print(p_logfc)
  cat("\n\n")

  # Correlation summary
  cor_test <- cor.test(nmd_logfc_dist$ptc_distance, nmd_logfc_dist$mean_logFC,
                        method = "spearman")
  cor_summary <- data.frame(
    n = nrow(nmd_logfc_dist),
    spearman_rho = round(cor_test$estimate, 3),
    cor_p = cor_test$p.value
  )
  cat("**Columns:** **n** = NMD comparator isoforms (all_samples) with both meta-analysis logFC and stop-to-EJC distance; ")
  cat("**spearman_rho** = Spearman correlation between distance and mean logFC; ")
  cat("**cor_p** = p-value for the correlation.\n\n")
  knitr::kable(cor_summary,
               caption = "Correlation: Stop-to-EJC Distance vs Mean logFC (mashr meta-analysis, all_samples)") |> print()
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### PTC Position Metrics: Which Best Predicts NMD Response?

The loess curve above suggests a non-linear relationship between stop codon distance and
logFC. To better understand what drives NMD efficiency, we compare three ways of measuring
PTC position using all_samples NMD comparators with mashr meta-analysis logFC:

- **PTC distance (nt)**: Raw nucleotide distance from stop codon to last EJC (truncated to 0–2000 nt to focus on the NMD-relevant range).
- **% CDS position**: Position of the PTC within the ORF as a percentage (`ptc_distance / orf_length * 100`), capped at 100%. Values that would exceed 100% arise when the distance from PTC to last EJC is longer than the ORF itself (i.e., many exons of 3' UTR lie downstream of an early PTC); these are set to 100%.
- **N downstream EJCs**: Number of exon-exon junctions downstream of the stop codon.

For each metric we fit a generalized additive model (GAM) to capture non-linear effects,
plus linear and quadratic models for comparison. All models are restricted to PTC+ isoforms
(distance > 50 nt) in the all_samples NMD comparison using mashr meta-analysis logFC.

```{r sec5-ptc-position-metrics, fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
# Merge PTC features with meta-analysis logFC for all_samples NMD comparators
as_comp_ids <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles$comparator_isoform_id

ptc_as <- ptc[ptc$isoform_id %in% as_comp_ids, ]
as_merged <- merge(meta_logfc[meta_logfc$txid %in% as_comp_ids, ], ptc_as,
                    by.x = "txid", by.y = "isoform_id")
as_merged <- as_merged[!is.na(as_merged$ptc_distance) & !is.na(as_merged$orf_length) &
                         as_merged$orf_length > 0, ]
as_merged$pct_cds_distance <- pmin(100, 100 * as_merged$ptc_distance / as_merged$orf_length)
as_merged$logFC <- as_merged$mean_logFC
as_ptc_pos <- as_merged[as_merged$has_ptc == TRUE, ]
```

```{r sec5-ptc-panel-plot, fig.height=5, fig.width=12}
if (has_ggplot2 && nrow(as_ptc_pos) > 0) {
  # PTC distance panel: restrict to 0-2000 nt
  dist_df <- data.frame(metric = "PTC distance (nt)", value = as_ptc_pos$ptc_distance,
                         logFC = as_ptc_pos$logFC)
  dist_df <- dist_df[dist_df$value <= 2000, ]

  ptc_long <- rbind(
    dist_df,
    data.frame(metric = "% CDS position", value = as_ptc_pos$pct_cds_distance,
               logFC = as_ptc_pos$logFC),
    data.frame(metric = "N downstream EJCs", value = as_ptc_pos$n_downstream_ejcs,
               logFC = as_ptc_pos$logFC)
  )
  ptc_long$metric <- factor(ptc_long$metric,
    levels = c("PTC distance (nt)", "% CDS position", "N downstream EJCs"))

  p_panel <- ggplot(ptc_long, aes(x = value, y = logFC)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.5, color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_x") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = sprintf("all_samples NMD Comparators (PTC+, n = %d): Mean logFC vs PTC Position Metrics",
                         nrow(as_ptc_pos)),
         subtitle = "mashr meta-analysis mean logFC (DD, AT, DO_ALI, FB, MV)",
         x = "Metric value", y = "Mean logFC (mashr, 5 conditions)")
  print(p_panel)
}
```

```{r sec5-ejc-boxplot, fig.height=5, fig.width=9}
if (has_ggplot2 && nrow(as_ptc_pos) > 0) {
  ejc_counts <- as_ptc_pos |>
    count(n_downstream_ejcs) |>
    mutate(label = paste0("n=", n))

  p_box <- ggplot(as_ptc_pos, aes(x = factor(n_downstream_ejcs), y = logFC)) +
    geom_violin(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_text(data = ejc_counts,
              aes(x = factor(n_downstream_ejcs),
                  y = max(as_ptc_pos$logFC) + 0.3, label = label),
              size = 2.8) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = "all_samples NMD Comparators: Mean logFC by Number of Downstream EJCs",
         subtitle = "mashr meta-analysis mean logFC rises sharply from 1-4 EJCs, then plateaus",
         x = "Number of downstream EJCs", y = "Mean logFC (mashr, 5 conditions)")
  print(p_box)
}
```

```{r sec5-gam-comparison, results='asis'}
if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE) && nrow(as_ptc_pos) > 0) {
  n_ejc_unique <- length(unique(as_ptc_pos$n_downstream_ejcs))

  # GAM models
  gam_dist <- mgcv::gam(logFC ~ s(ptc_distance), data = as_ptc_pos)
  gam_pct  <- mgcv::gam(logFC ~ s(pct_cds_distance), data = as_ptc_pos)
  gam_ejc  <- mgcv::gam(logFC ~ s(n_downstream_ejcs, k = min(n_ejc_unique, 10)),
                          data = as_ptc_pos)
  gam_comb <- mgcv::gam(logFC ~ s(ptc_distance) +
                           s(n_downstream_ejcs, k = min(n_ejc_unique, 10)),
                          data = as_ptc_pos)

  # Linear and quadratic models
  lm_dist_lin <- lm(logFC ~ ptc_distance, data = as_ptc_pos)
  lm_pct_lin  <- lm(logFC ~ pct_cds_distance, data = as_ptc_pos)
  lm_ejc_lin  <- lm(logFC ~ n_downstream_ejcs, data = as_ptc_pos)
  lm_dist_q   <- lm(logFC ~ poly(ptc_distance, 2), data = as_ptc_pos)
  lm_pct_q    <- lm(logFC ~ poly(pct_cds_distance, 2), data = as_ptc_pos)
  lm_ejc_q    <- lm(logFC ~ poly(n_downstream_ejcs, 2), data = as_ptc_pos)

  model_comparison <- data.frame(
    metric = c(rep("ptc_distance (nt)", 3), rep("pct_cds_distance (%)", 3),
               rep("n_downstream_ejcs", 3), "combined (dist + ejcs)"),
    model = c(rep(c("Linear", "Quadratic", "GAM"), 3), "GAM"),
    R_squared = round(c(
      summary(lm_dist_lin)$r.squared, summary(lm_dist_q)$r.squared,
        summary(gam_dist)$r.sq,
      summary(lm_pct_lin)$r.squared, summary(lm_pct_q)$r.squared,
        summary(gam_pct)$r.sq,
      summary(lm_ejc_lin)$r.squared, summary(lm_ejc_q)$r.squared,
        summary(gam_ejc)$r.sq,
      summary(gam_comb)$r.sq
    ), 3),
    AIC = round(c(
      AIC(lm_dist_lin), AIC(lm_dist_q), AIC(gam_dist),
      AIC(lm_pct_lin), AIC(lm_pct_q), AIC(gam_pct),
      AIC(lm_ejc_lin), AIC(lm_ejc_q), AIC(gam_ejc),
      AIC(gam_comb)
    ), 0)
  )
  knitr::kable(model_comparison,
               caption = sprintf("Model Comparison: PTC Position Metrics vs Mean logFC (all_samples, n = %d PTC+ isoforms)",
                                  nrow(as_ptc_pos))) |> print()
}
```

The number of downstream exon-exon junctions (`n_downstream_ejcs`) is the strongest single
predictor of NMD response magnitude. Normalizing by CDS length
actually weakens the signal --- the absolute number of downstream junctions matters more than
the relative position within the transcript. The relationship is non-linear: logFC rises
sharply from 1 to ~4 downstream EJCs and then plateaus, consistent with EJC-based NMD
surveillance having diminishing returns beyond a threshold number of junctions. Quadratic
terms are highly significant for all three metrics, confirming the non-linear pattern.
